name: Earth mass M_earth = 5.9722e24 kg (ladder.M_EARTH)

source.located: No single paper: M_E in kg is a derived measurement, M_E = GM_E / G. GM_E: IAU 2009 system (Luzum et al. 2011, Celest. Mech. Dyn. Astr. 110, 293 -- no arXiv copy, NAMED-NOT-READ); nominal (GM)^N_E = 3.986004e14 m^3 s^-2 READ in Prsa et al. 2016, IAU 2015 Resolution B3 (arXiv:1605.09788) Table 1 and sec 4; measured GM_E = 398600.4419(2) km^3 s^-2 READ-VIA-RESTATEMENT in Jentschura 2026 (arXiv:2609.09485) p.3 (citing Dunn & Torrence 1999, GRL 26, 1489, and DE440, Park et al. 2021). G: CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787) Table XXXII G = 6.67430(15)e-11, u_r 2.2e-5, identical to CODATA 2018 (sec I.B.11, sec XIV, sec XV.A) -- READ.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1605.09788 (IAU B3), 2409.03787 (CODATA 2022), 2609.09485 (restates GM_E and DE440 GM_E). An alphaXiv title lookup for Luzum 2011 resolved instead to Kaplan 2015 (arXiv:1511.01546), which cites Luzum 2011 but does not print GM_E; so the IAU 2009 GM_E best estimate is NAMED-NOT-READ and its measured value is taken from the 2026 restatement.

published_statement: IAU 2015 B3 (Prsa 2016 sec 3, rec. 2, 4, 5; Table 1): '1 (GM)^N_E = 3.986 004 x 10^14 m^3 s^-2' ... 'that if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of the Newtonian constant G should be specified in the publication'; sec 2: 'the uncertainty in G is five orders of magnitude larger than the uncertainty in GM'. CODATA 2022 Table XXXII: 'Newtonian constant of gravitation G 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2, 2.2 x 10^-5'; sec I.B.11: 'the 2022 and 2018 recommended values of G are therefore identical'. Jentschura 2026 p.3: 'mu = G M = 398600.4419(2) km^3/S^2, with an uncertainty of 5 x 10^-10'. Hence M_E = GM_E/G = 5.97217(13) x 10^24 kg (computed here).
published_hypotheses: H1 (IAU B3 rec. 5): an SI mass exists only as (GM)/G, and the G used must be stated; the kg value inherits u_r(G) = 2.2e-5, not u_r(GM) = 5e-10.

H2 (IAU B3 rec. 2 / sec 4): GM_E is the geocentric gravitational constant (Earth including atmosphere and oceans, excluding the Moon), referred to a stated time scale (TCG/TT vs TCB/TDB); the nominal value is rounded to the precision at which TCB and TDB values agree.
H3 (IAU B3 rec. 1-2): the nominal (GM)^N_E is a conversion constant, not the physical property; symbols like GM_E denote actual estimates with uncertainties.
H4 (CODATA 2022 sec XIV, XV.A): G is the weighted mean of 16 mutually inconsistent measurements with an expansion factor 3.9 applied; no new G datum entered 2022.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H1 (G must be stated) at ladder.py:63 (M_EARTH = 5.9722e24 given as a bare kg value with no G or GM cited). Mitigated, not absent: the same file's G = 6.67430e-11 (ladder.py:54; ledger.py:331 labels it CODATA 2018) is the G that reproduces 5.9722e24 from GM_E, and G*M_EARTH matches GM_E to 5.3e-6 (the 5-s.f. rounding). Computed, not presumed.

STATUS DRIFT at formation.py:359, 882, 1133: ladder.py:43 declares 'Astrophysical and engineering figures are RECALLED, not read, and marked' (and :44 'no claim rests on their third digit'), but M_EARTH at ladder.py:63 carries no individual mark (the '--- RECALLED, not read ---' marker at ladder.py:68 heads SOURCES, below it), and formation.py imports it with no status word into a product whose other factor is labelled 'READ, Anglada 2017 sec 1' (formation.py:452). The product at formation.py:882/1133 is therefore READ x RECALLED, printed without that distinction.

ADDED (implicit) at formation.py:452/882: that the 'M_earth' unit in which Anglada-Escude et al. 2016 / Anglada et al. 2017 state m_p sin i = 1.3 M_earth is the same kg value as ladder.M_EARTH. Not stated in the tree; any plausible difference in the papers' conversion constant is <= ~1e-4 relative, 22 orders below the margin of the use.

No drift on H2/H3/H4 that affects the use: the tree uses an actual-estimate kg value (not the nominal), to 5 s.f., where time-scale (1.6e-8) and G-inconsistency (~5.5e-4 full spread of the 16 G inputs) effects are below or at the 4th significant figure.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What was lacking is real and documented: G is the least well known constant, its 16 inputs are mutually inconsistent (expansion factor 3.9, residuals up to 7.7 before expansion, CODATA 2022 sec XIV/XVI.C.2), and no new G datum has entered since 2018; the IAU itself refused to put a kg value on the Earth's mass for this reason (B3 rec. 5). So the kg value is genuinely data-limited at ~2e-5 (formal) to ~5.5e-4 (full spread of the G inputs). Evidence that having the missing data would NOT change the tree's conclusion: the only conclusion resting on M_E here is formation.py's '1.3 M_E exceeds a 749 kg threshold', which holds by 22.0 orders of magnitude; its elasticity in M_E is exactly 1 (sympy), so a G error would have to be ~1e22-fold to matter, while the whole historical G spread moves log10(ratio) by < 1e-4. GM_E itself (the directly measured quantity) is known to 5e-10 and two independent determinations (SLR and DE440) agree after the time-scale conversion. Verdict on M's hypothesis for this result: the data lack is present in the source (G) but does not reach the use.
grade_evidence: Re-derivation agrees: GM_E/G with CODATA 2018 = CODATA 2022 G gives 5.972168(134)e24 kg, which rounds to the tree's 5.9722e24 (0.23 sigma). The only moved/contested datum (G: CODATA 2014 vs 2018, and the 3.9-expanded inconsistency among G inputs) shifts M_E at the 4th-5th significant figure; the tree's use (formation.py:882, 1133: Proxima b m sin i x M_E over stockgate's 749 kg threshold, log10 = 22.0155) is invariant under it (computed). Hypothesis drifts are recorded (H1 'state your G' dropped at ladder.py:63 but satisfied by ladder.py:54; RECALLED status of ladder.py:43 not carried into formation.py) and none shrinks the class on which the tree uses the value. Not NARROWED: no hypothesis the tree drops is one the use needs. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the conclusion does not move with the moved datum.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a tree use of M_EARTH that needs more than ~4 significant figures in kg (then the unstated G, H1, and the G-input inconsistency become load-bearing) -- ladder.py:303's 4-decimal pin 22.5871 is already at that edge (22.5872 in the G-free form) but is a selftest pin, not a claim. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a future G determination differing from 6.67430e-11 by > ~1e-4 relative would change the 5th s.f. of M_E (no effect on formation.py's verdict). To WRONG: only a demonstration that GM_E or G is off by many orders of magnitude, for which there is no evidence. The READ status of the IAU 2009 GM_E best estimate (Luzum 2011) would rise from NAMED-NOT-READ if its text became readable here; the grade would not move.
